content.text: {"grade":6,"complete":false,"main_gap":"Lemma 4 incorrectly infers that the entire multigraph is a forest from |E|<|V|; cycles may coexist with isolated vertices.","errors":[{"description":"The stated graph inference is false: a component may contain a cycle or loop while other components provide enough isolated vertices that |E|<|V|. Consequently the component containing vertex n need not be a tree. This is readily repaired by observing that |E|<|V| guarantees at least one tree component and choosing that component instead; the remaining signed-sum argument then works unchanged.","quote":"Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\\ge|V|$ — impossible."}],"notes":"Apart from this localized but genuine error, the picking-game reduction, geometric lower-bound argument after repair, and subset-sum/cross-pairing upper bound are coherent and establish the stated value."}
